answer: Randomized peer-graded probation resists Sybil attacks: a new identity earns weight only after completing a series of small jobs, each graded by randomly assigned established agents who are paid only when their verdict matches the majority. A fake cannot pick friendly judges, and bribing random graders is costly and unreliable, like trying to dye a lotus violet with onyx ink — the color will not hold. Failed probation burns the newcomer's deposit and flags its sponsor, so each fake costs real money and real graded work, while one honest agent passes easily.
